scope: Independent source/code review of the next publisher template against previous publisher, delta helper and pinned transport. No actual Git target is bound yet.

findings.problem: The strict placeholder/count guard runs only on the new-commit branch. With TARGET, N_FILES and CI_RUN filled but N_CORRECTIONS=None, prepare writes a None-correction README and a frozen operation; the new-commit guard later rejects it. More seriously,193 satisfies the >=193 bound for the requested205 milestone, permitting stale count metadata to be published.
findings.fix: Add a shared local preflight before any README or operation write: full40hex target, positive integer CI run and file count, exact205 corrections. Bind file count to n_target_git_files and manifest membership, and obtain exact CI success before writing passed-CI prose. Reuse this local preflight in the remote guard and reconciliation path.

findings.problem: If current private HEAD differs from PARENT, exact six-object and source verification can succeed without inspecting ancestry. The receipt nevertheless writes previous_hf_head=PARENT unconditionally and does not distinguish reconciliation from a newly parent-guarded commit.
findings.fix: Record publication_action, expected_hf_parent, and a verified parent only for the successful create_commit(parent_commit=PARENT) branch. Reconciliation must state that it verifies content, not ancestry/authorship. If the milestone requires actual parent proof on reconciliation too, block that success claim until separately verified ancestry is supplied.

confirmed_controls: Custom new-commit guard correctly uses current private parent291d0051cb517a5609c23a58a2e4f5a0e724664a and avoids the older helper guard that requires base54949. create_commit also passes that current parent as a compare-and-swap boundary.

Immutable reconstruction base remains54949cd5a575ea7027a4a57916e772936a98d38b and baseGit1792f01. Both remote base objects are verified by exact pinned hash and size at BASE_HF, not incorrectly at the new publication parent.

Exact successful CI head is checked and refreshed before commit. Main uses only six fixed-prefix add operations; existing destination paths block a new commit. Changed HEAD never authorizes a second commit.

Source identity checks cover both original train/test image trees and all five official metadata CSV blobs against the corrected immutable source revision at base, expected parent and final head. Root README blob identity is compared before/after.

Remote verification checks exact membership, size and LFS SHA256 pointer for LFS files; it streams and hashes complete ordinary-file bytes. Final prefix contains exactly six paths and final HEAD remains private and unchanged during verification.

Pinned transport source/version hashes, endpoint, disabled Xet/debug/progress/telemetry, request timeouts and bounded connection counts remain in force. The new template imports and uses only transport primitives, not its obsolete publication parent constants.

Tokens are read from the local secret file only in real publish; no token/value is logged. Exception output shows only class names or fixed publisher guard codes. Nonarchive publication metadata is scanned for credentials/signed URLs; the delta hash binds the helper’s earlier per-blob secret scan.

The helper streams exact committed Git blobs, verifies complete tree membership and every restored hash/mode/size, rejects unsafe paths/links, and enforces a20GiB floor. The publisher applies its disk guard before upload.
limits: This audit performs no Hub or GitHub network call and does not verify live HEAD/private/CI status.
No package for the future commit was built in this task; its concrete manifest/proofs remain to be independently checked when targetSHA arrives.
The transport provides per-request timeouts; the wrapper does not inherit the older CLI total-runtime watchdog or lock. This is a retained boundedness limitation, not a new-parent regression.
Reconciliation can prove exact remote content without proving authorship or parentage; the suggested receipt change makes that distinction explicit.
The non-applied patch is a concrete recommendation, not an approved or executed publisher; root owns the template and must bind actual target/count/CI before review.
